signals.entity: AMLA (all EU footprint banks: AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, EL, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: AMLR Art.28(1) obliged AMLA to submit the Customer Due Diligence RTS (Regulatory Technical Standard - binding Level-2 detail rules) to the Commission by 10/07/2026. As at 27/08/2026 AMLA's own Regulatory Instruments register still shows the Art.28(1) CDD RTS and the Art.19(9) RTS (criteria for identifying business relationships, occasional and linked transactions and lower thresholds) as 'consultation closed', with NO final report published; the register's finalised list covers only ITS 15(3) AMLAR, RTS 53(10) AMLD, ITS 81(1) AMLR, ITS 41(2) AMLAR, ITS 31(2) AMLD, RTS 40(2) AMLD, RTS 12(7) AMLAR. The CDD RTS is the instrument that fixes reliable independent verification sources and the attributes required of electronic identification means and qualified trust services for onboarding.
signals.source_name: AMLA — Regulatory Instruments register (page last updated 21/07/2026); AMLR Art.28(1) text
signals.implies: The single most important spec for Printec's digital onboarding/eKYC line (Namirial) and for CDD data capture in IMTF Siron is still draft. Footprint banks must scope re-platforming against draft text with <11 months to 10/07/2027, which favours vendors who can ship a configurable rules layer rather than hard-coded CDD flows. Also lands Printec Namirial + Siron in the same deal.
signals.likelihood: Very high that banks scope CDD/eKYC remediation in the FY2027 budget round now open; moderate that the RTS text shifts materially before OJ publication
signals.followup: Watch AMLA's Regulatory Instruments register weekly for the Art.28(1) and Art.19(9) final reports, and EUR-Lex for the first Commission Delegated Regulation adopting an AMLA RTS.

signals.signal: Four AMLA public consultations are open: draft Guidelines on ongoing monitoring of a business relationship (Art.26(5) AMLR) launched 03/06/2026, closing 03/09/2026 (final Guidelines expected Q4-2026); ITS on the reporting format for suspicions and transaction records launched 02/07/2026, closing 20/09/2026; RTS on risk-profile assessment for non-financial obliged entities launched 13/07/2026, closing 27/09/2026; RTS on cross-border information exchange between FIUs (Financial Intelligence Units) under Art.31(3) AMLD6 launched 06/07/2026, closing 06/10/2026. The ongoing-monitoring Guidelines set general principles, rules on keeping customer information up to date, and a transaction-and-activity monitoring framework applying across financial and non-financial sectors.
signals.implies: The ongoing-monitoring Guidelines are the functional specification for transaction monitoring — the direct hook for INETCO (real-time transaction monitoring) and IMTF Siron (AML/KYC, customer-data refresh and alerting). Baseline flagged the 03/09/2026 date as 'partially-confirmed'; it is now confirmed against AMLA's own page, and three further AMLA consultations with hard September/October 2026 dates are added.
signals.likelihood: High — final Guidelines Q4-2026 give banks ~6 months to configure before 10/07/2027
signals.followup: Retrieve the final ongoing-monitoring Guidelines when published in Q4-2026 and map clause-by-clause to INETCO and Siron capability.

signals.signal: AMLA published the Final Report on draft RTS under Art.53(10) AMLD6 on pecuniary sanctions, administrative measures and periodic penalty payments. It was consulted 09/02/2026-09/03/2026 (91 responses) and states the draft RTS 'will be submitted to the European Commission for adoption before being published in the Official Journal'. Mechanism: supervisors assess gravity against a fixed indicator list, classify each breach into one of four severity categories, then set the sanction against listed criteria; the RTS also fixes right-to-be-heard, a limitation period for collecting periodic penalty payments, and minimum content of the imposing decision.
signals.source_name: AMLA — Final Report, Draft RTS under Article 53(10) of Directive (EU) 2024/1640 (PDF); publication reported 08/07/2026 by the Hellenic Bank Association
signals.implies: Harmonised, formula-driven AML fines across BoG, CBC, BNB, CNB-CZ, NBS-SK, HNB, MNB, BNR, BSI and FMA/OeNB raise the expected cost of a monitoring or CDD failure and make evidence/auditability the deciding purchase criterion — Siron case management and INETCO audit trails. Not a standalone product sale; it is the business case for the ones above.
signals.likelihood: High — Commission adoption then OJ publication expected before AMLR application
signals.followup: Track EUR-Lex for the adopting Delegated Regulation and its entry into force.

signals.entity: AMLA / national supervisors (BNB, HNB, CBC, CNB-CZ, NBS-SK, MNB, BNR, BSI, BoG, FMA-AT)
signals.signal: AMLA's selection pipeline for direct supervision: press release 12/05/2026 published the reporting package (template + interpretative note) for national competent authorities to collect eligibility data from obliged entities; a public webinar ran 10/06/2026; national supervisors had to submit the data to AMLA by 15/08/2026; the provisional list of eligible obliged entities is to be finalised end-September 2026. Eligibility test: financial institutions or groups operating in six or more EU Member States. A second data collection runs in early 2027 against 31/12/2026 reference data; selection of up to 40 entities takes place in 2027; direct AMLA supervision starts 2028. AMLA's source does not name individual institutions.
signals.source_name: AMLA — 'AMLA takes next step toward 2027 selection of entities for direct supervision'
signals.implies: Cross-border groups with footprint subsidiaries (Erste, Raiffeisen Bank International, UniCredit, OTP, NLB, Intesa Sanpaolo all operate well beyond six Member States — Printec's own inference, not stated by AMLA) will be data-tested twice inside 12 months. Group-level AML data lineage and consistent CDD/monitoring records across subsidiaries become a procurement driver — Siron group deployments plus INETCO for transaction-level evidence. Budget commits in the FY2027 cycle now open (Sept-Nov 2026).
signals.likelihood: High that the provisional list lands end-Sept 2026; the named-entity list is not public
signals.followup: Check at end-September 2026 whether AMLA publishes or leaks the provisional eligible list, and confirm which footprint groups' NCAs (HNB, BNB, MNB, BNR, CNB-CZ, NBS-SK, BoG, CBC) submitted.

signals.signal: AMLA launched a survey of Electronic Money Institutions and Payment Service Providers on the Central Contact Point framework (Art.45(9) AMLD and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/1108), open until 15/09/2026, as preparatory work for future RTS under Art.41(2) AMLD. Separately the EBA's reporting framework Release 4.4 contains a public working draft of the data model and taxonomy that will support the 2027 AMLA eligibility data collection, assessing whether 2026 provisionally-eligible entities still meet the criteria as at 31/12/2026; feedback closed 24/08/2026.
signals.source_name: FIAU Malta (national FIU) summary of the AMLA CCP survey and EBA Release 4.4
signals.implies: A fixed EBA taxonomy for AML eligibility reporting means footprint banks need machine-generated, schema-conformant AML data as at 31/12/2026 — a reporting/data-extract workstream on top of Siron, and an argument for replacing spreadsheet-based AML MI. Payment institutions in the footprint (including terminal/acquiring clients) are separately in scope of the CCP survey.
signals.followup: Obtain the EBA Release 4.4 AML taxonomy files and confirm the final 2027 collection window.

signals.entity: European Commission — AMLD6 transposition monitoring (Croatia, Cyprus, Greece, Slovakia)
signals.signal: Commission transposition tracker for Directive (EU) 2024/1640 (AMLD6), page updated 07/08/2026: against the 10/07/2025 tranche deadline, CROATIA has communicated NO transposition measures and SLOVAKIA only PARTIAL measures; Austria, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czechia, Greece, Hungary, Romania and Slovenia are recorded as having communicated full measures. Ten Member States have infringement proceedings pending for lack, delay or incompleteness of notification — in the footprint these are CROATIA, CYPRUS, GREECE and SLOVAKIA. The wider AMLD6 calendar is staggered: Art.74 by 10/07/2025; Arts.11, 12, 13 and 15 (beneficial-ownership and bank-account registers) by 10/07/2026; the general deadline 10/07/2027; Art.18 (interconnection of bank-account registers) by 10/07/2029 — the staggered dates come from Art.78 and could NOT be verified against EUR-Lex this run (see access issues).
signals.source_name: European Commission — Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Directive VI, transposition monitoring
signals.implies: Late transposers compress their own banks' delivery windows: Croatian and Slovak banks (Zagrebacka/UniCredit, PBZ/Intesa, Erste Croatia, OTP Croatia; SLSP, VUB, Tatra) will get national AML rules late and then face the same 10/07/2027 AMLR date, which historically produces rushed, vendor-led remediation — the best entry point for Siron/Namirial displacement. Cyprus and Greece infringements are also a live check on the carried Cyprus verification debts.
signals.likelihood: High — infringement pressure typically forces national laws within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Monitor the Croatian and Slovak gazettes (Narodne novine; Zbierka zakonov) for the AMLD6 transposition acts, and re-check this Commission page monthly.

signals.entity: Bosnia & Herzegovina — banking sector (Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, Raiffeisen Bank BiH, Sparkasse Bank BiH, UniCredit Bank BiH, NLB Banka)
signals.signal: At its plenary of 17-19/06/2026 the FATF placed Bosnia & Herzegovina back on the list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring ('grey list'), alongside Iraq; Algeria and Namibia were removed, leaving 22 jurisdictions. BiH made a high-level political commitment to work with FATF and MONEYVAL; its action plan requires deeper ML/TF risk understanding, systematic use of international cooperation, and proportionate, dissuasive and effective SANCTIONING OF THE BANKING SECTOR. The Banking Agency of the Federation of BiH publicly stated the listing does not call bank stability into question. CAUTION: the FATF's own pages (increased-monitoring June 2026 and the plenary outcomes) returned HTTP 403 behind Cloudflare to every route tried this run, so the FATF wording above is corroborated from BiH press and EU material, not read on FATF's site — treat as press-tier until re-verified.
signals.source_name: Klix.ba (BiH) — 'FATF uvrstio BiH na listu drzava pod pojacanim nadzorom' [FATF places BiH on the list of countries under increased monitoring]; FBA statement via HMS.ba
signals.implies: Two effects. (a) Inside BiH, banks face an explicit FATF demand for effective sanctioning, which drives supervisory inspections and forces monitoring/CDD upgrades — direct Siron/INETCO opportunity at Intesa, Raiffeisen and Sparkasse, the three banks already named as the only participants in BiH's domestic instant scheme. (b) Across the rest of the footprint, correspondent and cross-border flows to BiH move into enhanced due diligence, adding screening/monitoring load at every footprint bank with BiH exposure. Watch for BiH being re-added to the EU high-risk third-country list (it was delisted in the Jan-2026 update), which would make EDD legally mandatory EU-wide.
signals.likelihood: High that CBBH/FBA/ABRS tighten AML supervision within 12 months
signals.followup: Re-verify against the FATF primary page via an operator-fetched copy; watch the Commission for a Delegated Regulation re-adding BiH to the Annex of Delegated Reg (EU) 2016/1675.

signals.signal: At the June 2026 FATF plenary the FATF made the initial determination that BULGARIA has substantially completed its October-2023 action plan and warrants an on-site assessment — the last procedural step before removal from the grey list. Monaco was given the same determination. Same access caveat as above: FATF's own page was 403/Cloudflare-blocked to all routes this run.
signals.source_name: ComplyAdvantage summary of FATF plenary June 2026 outcomes (secondary; FATF primary blocked)
signals.implies: If the on-site succeeds, Bulgaria could be delisted at the October 2026 plenary. That REMOVES a driver of enhanced screening spend at Bulgarian banks (UniCredit Bulbank, DSK/OTP, UBB/KBC, Postbank, Fibank) just as euro-adoption and AMLR spend competes for the same budget — so pitch AML tooling in Bulgaria on the AMLR 10/07/2027 deadline, not on grey-list risk.
signals.likelihood: Moderate-to-high delisting at the Oct-2026 plenary
signals.followup: Confirm at the October 2026 FATF plenary; source the FATF statement directly.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine — JSC Raiffeisen Bank (Ukraine), JSC Bank Ukrainian Capital
signals.signal: NBU published its July-2026 enforcement round on 07/08/2026: measures against 2 banks and 19 non-bank financial institutions for AML/CFT (PVK/FT) and currency-law breaches. JSC RAIFFEISEN BANK was fined UAH 16,100,000 for improper customer due diligence (Art.8(2)(4) of the AML Law), failure to apply a risk-based approach (Art.7(1)-(2)), failure to manage risks arising from new and existing information products, business practices or technologies INCLUDING THOSE ENABLING NON-FACE-TO-FACE TRANSACTIONS (Art.8(2)(25)), late reporting of threshold transactions, and failure to supply the NBU with complete information; plus a written warning for not applying additional PEP measures and for internal AML documents lacking procedures sufficient for effective risk management. JSC Bank Ukrainian Capital was fined a total of UAH 42,500,000 (UAH 40.5m for improper organisation of primary financial monitoring). Both banks were also cited under para.4 of NBU Board Resolution No.37 of 04/04/2024 for FAILING TO CONFIGURE AND AUTOMATE the generation of the standard response forms in Annex 1 to Regulation No.90.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — 'NBU v lypni zastosuvav zakhody vplyvu do 2 bankiv i 19 nebankivskykh finustanov...' [In July the NBU applied enforcement measures to 2 banks and 19 non-bank financial institutions for breaches in financial monitoring and currency law]
signals.implies: The NBU is fining banks explicitly for NOT AUTOMATING AML response generation and for weak non-face-to-face channel risk management. That is a named, regulator-evidenced product gap Printec sells into: IMTF Siron / FICO for CDD, PEP screening and case automation, INETCO for real-time transaction monitoring and threshold-transaction detection, Namirial for compliant remote onboarding. Raiffeisen is a footprint group account. Budget commits immediately — remediation plans follow NBU orders within one supervisory cycle.
signals.likelihood: Very high — NBU publishes enforcement monthly and remediation is mandatory
signals.followup: Pull the August-2026 and September-2026 NBU enforcement notices; approach Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine and PrivatBank (existing NCR recycler customer) with the automation finding.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine — all Ukrainian banks
signals.signal: NBU Board Resolution No.81 of 15/07/2026 'On approving Amendments to the Regulation on banks' financial monitoring' (amending Regulation No.65 of 19/05/2020) entered into force 17/07/2026. It widens the permitted methods of remote client verification: an identity document may be presented by an accompanying or authorised person, or held up by a bank employee performing verification where the client cannot present it; and the client's consent to photo capture may be evidenced by AUDIO/VIDEO RECORDING where a handwritten or electronic signature is impossible. Under the Law on financial-inclusion development, a financial-inclusion bank may also engage a commercial agent to establish the beneficiary of a transaction and to carry out identification and verification under the same Regulation.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — 'Rozshyreno perelik sposobiv veryfikatsii bankamy kliientiv dlia tsilei finansovoi inkliuzii' [The list of client verification methods for financial-inclusion purposes has been expanded]; NBU Board Resolution No.81 of 15/07/2026
signals.implies: Ukraine has legalised video/photo-based remote KYC with agent-assisted verification — the exact envelope Printec's Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC stack fills, and it can be delivered through bank kiosks and self-service branches where a bank employee performs the capture. Combined with the July enforcement above (non-face-to-face channel risk), the same account needs onboarding AND monitoring. Budget: NBU rule already in force, so spend commits in the 2026-2027 planning round.
signals.followup: Obtain the consolidated text of Regulation No.65 as amended and map the capture/consent requirements to Namirial's video-KYC flow.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine — 2026 AML on-site inspection plan
signals.signal: NBU updated its 2026 plan of on-site inspections on financial monitoring, currency and sanctions legislation on 25/08/2026, having also published changes on 31/07/2026. In the published revisions LLC FC 'Solid Group' was removed following licence withdrawal and LLC 'Bank KD' was added with its inspection scheduled for Q4-2026; other revisions were technical renamings (LLC FC 'Finexpress' to LLC Payment Institution 'Finexpress'). The number of planned inspections and their timing otherwise stayed unchanged.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine news item 'Onovleno plan viyizdnykh perevirok z pytan finansovoho monitorynhu...' [The plan of on-site inspections on financial monitoring, currency and sanctions law compliance for 2026 has been updated], referenced from bank.gov.ua; detail via psm7.com and dtkt.ua
signals.implies: A named, dated inspection calendar is the cleanest sales trigger there is: institutions with a Q4-2026 slot must be able to evidence CDD files, PEP screening and transaction monitoring within weeks. Note: the NBU news item itself is JS-rendered and its direct URL could not be resolved this run — the item title and date are read from the 'related news' block of the Resolution No.81 page; the Bank KD detail is press-tier. Do not quote the inspection list to a client until the primary page is retrieved.
signals.likelihood: Certain — plan is published and binding
signals.followup: Retrieve the NBU inspection-plan page and the full 2026 list of inspected banks via an operator with a browser session.

signals.entity: Montenegro — Parliament / CBCG-supervised banks (CKB-OTP, NLB Banka, Erste Bank Montenegro, Hipotekarna banka, Lovcen banka)
signals.signal: Montenegro's Parliament adopted amendments to the Law on Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism reported to have entered into force on 12/05/2026, framed as delivering full implementation of FATF recommendations as requested by MONEYVAL and aligning with Regulation (EU) 2024/1624 (AMLR). The amendments are reported to cover governance and oversight, customer due diligence, CUSTOMER ONBOARDING, CUSTOMER MONITORING and restrictions on cash transactions. CAUTION: the law-firm source (BDK Advokati via CEE Legal Matters) is Cloudflare-blocked to tooling and the Sluzbeni list reference could not be pinned this run — an earlier amending law sits at Sluzbeni list CG 024/25 of 12/03/2025. Treat the 12/05/2026 date and the AMLR-alignment framing as UNVERIFIED against the gazette.
signals.source_name: CEE Legal Matters / BDK Advokati — 'Amendments to AML Legislation in Montenegro' (blocked to fetch tools; content from search index)
signals.implies: A non-EU footprint market voluntarily importing AMLR onboarding and monitoring standards is an early-mover market: five commercial banks, all mid-sized, none likely to build in-house. Maps to Namirial eKYC (onboarding) plus Siron (CDD/monitoring); cash-transaction restrictions additionally raise the case for recyclers/TCRs with automated cash-source recording. Budget window: 6-12 months from entry into force, i.e. now.
signals.likelihood: Moderate — the direction is clear, the exact dates are not verified
signals.followup: Pull the amending law from sluzbenilist.me and the CBCG's implementing decisions; confirm entry-into-force and any transitional compliance deadline for banks.

signals.entity: MONEYVAL / Serbia — APML and NBS-supervised banks
signals.signal: MONEYVAL adopted the 6th-round mutual evaluation report on SERBIA at its 70th Plenary in December 2025 — Serbia being the second country assessed under the 6th round — with publication announced for June 2026 and Serbia reported to be placed in enhanced follow-up. CAUTION: coe.int returned a Cloudflare block ('Attention Required') to every route tried this run, and apml.gov.rs's MONEYVAL page still lists only 2009-2010 documents; the publication date and the enhanced-follow-up status are therefore NOT confirmed against a primary source.
signals.source_name: Council of Europe MONEYVAL — 'Outcome of MONEYVAL 70th Plenary Meeting' and Serbia jurisdiction page (both Cloudflare-blocked; content from search index)
signals.implies: A 6th-round MER with enhanced follow-up puts sustained, dated pressure on Serbian banks' effectiveness — specifically transaction monitoring quality and STR usefulness, which are Immediate Outcome 4/6 findings and cannot be closed with policy documents alone. Direct hook for INETCO plus Siron at NBS-supervised banks; Raiffeisen Serbia and AikBank are existing Printec accounts (x-core, NCR recyclers).
signals.likelihood: High that NBS issues follow-up supervisory expectations within 12 months
signals.followup: Have an operator retrieve the MONEYVAL 6th-round Serbia MER PDF and the technical-compliance/effectiveness rating tables, then map the IO.4 findings to specific monitoring gaps.

signals.entity: European Commission / AMLA — whole EU footprint
signals.signal: No Commission Delegated or Implementing Regulation adopting any AMLA Level-2 instrument has yet been published in the Official Journal. AMLA's mandate was to deliver 23 RTS/ITS/Guidelines to the Commission by 10/07/2026; final reports so far cover risk-profile assessment (RTS Art.40(2) AMLD), selection for direct supervision (RTS Art.12(7) AMLAR), FIU-to-FIU formats (ITS Art.31(2) AMLD), FIU and AMLA reporting to the EPPO (ITS Art.81(1) AMLR, ITS Art.41(2) AMLAR), the sanctions RTS (Art.53(10) AMLD) and ITS Art.15(3) AMLAR — each of which states it 'will be submitted to the European Commission for adoption before being published in the Official Journal'. AMLR (Reg (EU) 2024/1624) applies 10/07/2027 regardless.
signals.source_name: AMLA — Regulatory Instruments register; AMLA Final Report RTS Art.53(10) 'Next steps'
signals.implies: With ~10.5 months to AMLR application and the binding Level-2 text not yet in the OJ, every footprint bank is scoping against drafts. Printec's commercial angle is configurability and speed-to-change: a Siron/Namirial/INETCO proposition sold as 'rules you can re-point when the OJ text lands' beats a fixed-scope integration. Budget must commit in the FY2027 cycle (Sept-Nov 2026) to leave any implementation runway at all.
signals.likelihood: Very high that Commission adoption slips into late 2026 / H1 2027, compressing bank delivery
signals.followup: Set a standing EUR-Lex watch on 'AMLA' delegated regulations; report the first OJ publication as a hard trigger.

Primary-first: AMLA's own consultation register, regulatory-instruments register and Final Report PDF (text extracted locally with pdfminer); the European Commission's AMLD6 transposition-monitoring page (updated 07/08/2026); the National Bank of Ukraine's news and normative pages fetched with a desktop User-Agent via curl after WebFetch 403s. Local-language sweep run in Ukrainian (bank.gov.ua, enforcement and Regulation No.65/No.81), Bosnian/Serbian/Croatian (klix.ba, hms.ba for the FBA statement, sluzbenilist/gov.me for Montenegro), Greek (Hellenic Bank Association AML activity page, which surfaced the 08/07/2026 Art.53(10) RTS publication and the 07/08/2026 AMLA CCP survey), Bulgarian (ZMIP internal-rules obligations — nothing new since 02/08/2026), Romanian (ONPCSB public-debate register — no 2026 AMLD6 transposition draft posted; latest items are 2022) and Serbian (APML MONEYVAL page — stale). Genuine gaps: (1) no primary read of the FATF June-2026 statements on BiH and Bulgaria — FATF is Cloudflare-blocked; (2) no primary read of the MONEYVAL 6th-round Serbia MER — coe.int Cloudflare-blocked; (3) EUR-Lex could not be read at all, so AMLD6 Art.78's staggered transposition dates (Art.74 10/07/2025; Arts.11/12/13/15 10/07/2026; general 10/07/2027; Art.18 10/07/2029) are reported from secondary sources and remain a verification debt — this is the same EUR-Lex block the baseline recorded against the DORA subcontracting RTS, and the desktop-User-Agent workaround did NOT defeat it (EUR-Lex returns HTTP 202 with a 2KB bot-challenge body); (4) no new national AML/CFT law found in AT, CZ, SK, SI, HU, CY, XK or AL since 02/08/2026 — the material national movement in the period is Croatia's and Slovakia's non-transposition of AMLD6 rather than new statutes. Nothing in this workstream touches data-subject-rights or personal-data-breach questions; the Montenegro and Ukraine onboarding items involve biometric/photo capture, and any deployment design there must be cleared with Printec's DPO / Compliance team before being pitched. All confidence capped at Medium per the single-agent rule; several rows are marked Low where only press or aggregator sources could be opened.
